From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jul 2025 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed indemnity language (draft)
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Team — draft highlights (will push as redline next):

1) Trigger carveout: "Third-party claim" means a claim alleging infringement arising from Redwood's models or services as delivered by Redwood. Claims arising from Customer Data used for training are excluded where Customer provides documented provenance and a manifest of data sources. (Reason: narrows scope to vendor-origin exposure.)

2) Notice & preservation: Add a clause requiring Customer to provide written notice within 30 days of becoming aware of a claim that could reasonably be expected to trigger indemnity; Redwood to appoint an initial evidence liaison (Redwood Ops/SRE) within 48 hours for triage; if litigation commences, parties will agree on a designated technical custodian and a shared secure artifact repository for sample artifacts. (Reason: reduces friction during triage and sets expectations.)

3) Insurance-first waterfall: Include procedural language that parties will seek recovery from applicable insurer(s) before drawing against contractual caps; specify that Redwood will reasonably cooperate with insurer subrogation. (Reason: protects balance-sheet while keeping process simple.)

4) Cooperation / control: Maintain Redwood's right to assume defense for covered claims but include a mutual cooperation paragraph and a requirement to obtain Customer consent for any settlement that admits liability or imposes payment obligations on Customer. (Reason: preserves commercial control.)

I'll prepare a redline for OrderForm_v3 reflecting the above and send it for Marcus/Laura review. Laura — when you confirm the Ops contact we'll include the contact block and an SLA for initial response (48 hours).

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
